column2: Wow if you have blind panic because of a crack in your phone screen, you might have other problems. I can understand being pissed, but holy shit, you just bought it, they'll replace it. It'll be okay. Get your old phone... oh right you just traded it in and rolled it into your new payment plan. The fact that this is normalized in the article says something about our society.
It is better clip bait to proclaim "blind panic" than to say "shit, I need to take this back for a replacement".
Only a married man can know the exquisite burning humiliation of breaking a brand new expensive tech toy while showing it off to one’s sceptical wife.
It mostly shows that people are spending well outside their means.

While I don't doubt many people are doing that, using the iPhone/Apple Upgrade Program does not immediately equate to that being the case. I always use the Upgrade program but I could buy the phone outright if I wanted but why would I? It's essentially a 0% interest loan if I buy the phone out at the end. Sure if you turn the phone in after a year (or two) you are leaving money on the table (vs selling it or repurposing it) but the Upgrade programs aren't only used by people spending outside their means.

The iPhone update program /was/ a great deal for a number of reasons. The current klarna incarnation pushes the value lever in the wrong direction, this being the first year I haven’t upgraded in probably a decade. I /could/ pay cash, but it was just as easy to use someone else’s money so why not?

My understanding is that while it's a loan->lease change, the TCO is the same under both plans. I might agree that the Klarna version feel scummier but it doesn't change the financials for me and it's still effectively a 0% interest loan. I set aside the full cost of the phone in my budgeting app on day 1 and then draw down from that category over the span of the loan/lease so it's effectively like I'm buying it but I get to park the money in a HYSA.
The TCO isn’t the same mostly because now you need to pay for AppleCare separately where before it was included.

There’s a good chance I’m wrong about this, but I thought they lowered the price to account for not including Apple Care? So you’re correct, it’s no longer included, but the price per month and total cost of ownership is the same?

In normal circumstances, one cannot return a phone with a broken screen; it's generally accidental damage rather than the design being unfit for purpose.

In this case, it's obviously a manufacturing or design flaw, but were I in these customers' shoes, I would be a little nervous on my way back to the AppleStore, too.

I think if I thought I’d wasted a paycheck on a broken gadget I’d feel blind panic for a second, I’d eventually think through the reality that they’ll probably cover such an obvious fault, but I’d still feel incredibly stupid for wasting my money at first.

Of course, that’s why i wouldn’t buy this thing in the first place, but i can empathise with those who were less willing to wait and see.
What does selling an old thing to buy a new thing say about our society?
